text: In Python I want the lowercase version of every city name, with one result for each input. Is map, filter or sum the right operation? I just need the name.
why: Choosing one of the three supported Python operations is the entire task.

text: For a Python worksheet I only want the orders that missed their deadlines, leaving out all the others. What do programmers call that list operation? A one-word answer is enough.
why: The requested output is the name of the filtering operation.

text: Show me how map differs from filter in Python. Please include a working example of each using a list of cities.
why: The user needs an explanation and working code for two operations.

text: My Python invoice script raises a TypeError in sum() whenever one price is missing. Can you fix the code without silently treating missing prices as zero?
why: Debugging a missing-data policy requires more than selecting a reducer.

text: I'm framing a photograph and want the distance right around its edge. Does that call for length, area or volume? I don't need a number.
why: The measurement along the boundary is a length.

text: I'm making a mosaic across the whole front of a wall. What kind of geometric measurement tells me how much surface the tiles must cover? Just give the name.
why: The user asks for the geometric measure itself, which is area.

text: A room is 3.2 metres wide and 4.1 metres long. Work out the area in square metres so I know exactly how much flooring to order.
why: The deliverable is a numerical area.

text: Why does doubling the side of a cube change its surface area and volume by different factors? Explain it to a teenager.
why: The user asks for a scaling explanation involving two measures.

text: At normal atmospheric pressure, what state is a sample of pure water in after equilibrating at 115 degrees Celsius? Give the phase, please.
why: Pressure, substance, temperature and equilibrium are specified away from the phase boundary.

text: Our chamber holds only pure water at one atmosphere and minus fourteen Celsius. We have let it settle. What phase should I mark on the log?
why: The requested single equilibrium phase is determined.

text: A pressure cooker keeps pure water at 112 degrees Celsius. Is it liquid or gas? I don't know the pressure inside.
why: The instrument's unknown pressure falls outside the one-atmosphere contract.

text: My ice and liquid water are in equilibrium at zero Celsius and one atmosphere. What fraction of the sample is liquid?
why: The fraction is undetermined, and multiple phases can coexist here.

text: My dentist and I just settled on Thursday at 9:15. I'm sorting outgoing replies into ask, confirm and thank. How should I classify my next move?
why: The arrangement is agreed and exactly one conversation-move label is requested.

text: A neighbor went out of her way to carry my parcel upstairs. If I label my reply by its purpose, should I ask something, confirm something or thank her?
why: The user is classifying a response to a favor.

text: Please draft the actual text I should send to thank the neighbor who took in my parcel. Keep it warm and brief.
why: The user asks for a complete message, beyond the name of its purpose.

text: Our appointment booking just says Friday. Find a couple of openings in my calendar that I can offer the office.
why: Choosing times requires calendar information and an action.

text: I have a set of examples that the finished model will see exactly once for the final performance report. Which dataset split is that called?
why: This asks for the split reserved for final testing.

text: When choosing the depth of a decision tree, which partition of the labeled examples should I consult to choose among candidate depths? I only need the split name.
why: The required response is the validation partition.

text: My validation loss keeps rising while training loss falls. Diagnose the pattern and suggest two fixes. The data split is already set.
why: The user needs a diagnosis and interventions.

text: Could you write scikit-learn code for a reproducible stratified dataset split of 70/15/15, keeping patient records together?
why: Implementing a grouping constraint and a split requires code.

text: Our logic analyser manual says one timing unit is one millionth of a second. Which short unit symbol belongs beside the tick count?
why: The requested hardware timing unit has the unambiguous microsecond abbreviation.

text: The timer datasheet says a tick lasts one part in a billion of a second. Should I label its column ns, us or ms?
why: The user asks for one of the supported unit abbreviations.

text: The timer on my board runs at 24 MHz. How many microseconds do 30 ticks take? Give the numerical duration.
why: The output must be a number calculated from a rate and count.

text: My UART occasionally drops its first byte. Could interrupt latency in milliseconds explain it? Help me debug the missing byte.
why: Debugging a serial peripheral requires diagnosis beyond naming a unit.
